_why: ONE table, two languages. `display_state()` lives in corral_core/sessions.py, and both web skins must mirror it in JavaScript -- the browser reduces events locally between polls, so it cannot ask the server what a pane means at the moment a permission card arrives. A mirror that is not pinned is a fork waiting to happen, so every case below is asserted against BOTH implementations: corral_core/test_display_state.py (python) and static/../selftest_display.mjs in each skin (javascript). Add a case here and both languages have to answer it.
_fields: pane = the duck-typed attributes display_state reads (state, pending, gate_hold, idle_s); unread = the caller's own knowledge; want = the display state.
_removal: deleted with display_state itself (DESIGN-5 S1, section 5).

cases.why: a fresh pane is working, not idle
a wedged adapter is still working, never idle -- the whole point of the uncertain state
IDLE_DISPLAY_S exactly: the boundary belongs to idle
read, and quiet for half an hour: this is what `idle` exists to say
an unread reply outranks the clock, however old
a pending card is needs-you EVEN THOUGH the raw state says ready
the runbook gate parked it: no card, but only a human releases it
a gate hold on a stale pane still wants the human, not `idle`
the raw needs-you state, with the card not yet in `pending`
a card outranks death: the core clears pending on exit, so where these overlap it is a bug and hiding it is worse
restored from disk, deliberately not running: idle, never dead
an enum value this function does not know is NOT claimed to be working -- the raw label is rendered beside it
no state at all (a stripped object): treated as starting
